questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In transition metal nitrosyl complexes, a linearly coordinated $\text{NO}$ ligand ($\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O} \approx 180^\circ$) compared to a bent $\text{NO}$ ligand ($\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O} \approx 120^\circ$) is formally regarded as
optionsEn: $\text{NO}^+$ (a $3\text{ e}^-$ neutral donor) with a higher $\nu_{\text{NO}}$ stretching frequency
$\text{NO}^+$ (a $1\text{ e}^-$ neutral donor) with a lower $\nu_{\text{NO}}$ stretching frequency
$\text{NO}^-$ (a $1\text{ e}^-$ neutral donor) with a higher $\nu_{\text{NO}}$ stretching frequency
$\text{NO}^-$ (a $3\text{ e}^-$ neutral donor) with a lower $\nu_{\text{NO}}$ stretching frequency
questions.explanationEn: Linear $\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ is isoelectronic with $\text{CO}$ and is formulated as $\text{NO}^+$ (donating $2\text{ e}^-$ in the ionic model or $3\text{ e}^-$ in the neutral model), retaining a high $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bond order ($\nu_{\text{NO}} \approx 1650\text{--}1950\text{ cm}^{-1}$). Bent $\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O}$ is formulated as $\text{NO}^-$ ($1\text{ e}^-$ neutral donor) with a lone pair on N and lower $\nu_{\text{NO}}$ ($\sim 1525\text{--}1720\text{ cm}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Using Wade-Mingos polyhedral skeletal electron pair theory, the neutral carbonyl cluster $\text{Os}_5(\text{CO})_{16}$ (atomic number of $\text{Os} = 76$) has a skeletal geometry classified as
optionsEn: *arachno* (butterfly, $n + 3 = 8$ skeletal electron pairs)
*hypho* (open chain, $n + 4 = 9$ skeletal electron pairs)
*closo* (trigonal bipyramidal, $n + 1 = 6$ skeletal electron pairs)
*nido* (square pyramidal, $n + 2 = 7$ skeletal electron pairs)
questions.explanationEn: For $\text{Os}_5(\text{CO})_{16}$ ($n = 5$), total valence electrons $\text{TVE} = 5(8) + 16(2) = 72\text{ e}^-$. Subtracting $12n = 60$ non-skeletal electrons leaves $72 - 60 = 12$ polyhedral skeletal electrons, i.e., $6$ skeletal electron pairs (SEPs). Since $\text{SEPs} = n + 1 = 6$, the cluster is *closo* with a $5$-vertex trigonal bipyramidal $\text{Os}_5$ core.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions between an aryl halide ($\text{Ar}-\text{X}$) and an organometallic nucleophile ($\text{R}-\text{M}$), the Suzuki-Miyaura coupling specifically employs
optionsEn: an organozinc reagent ($\text{R}-\text{ZnCl}$)
a terminal alkyne with a $\text{Cu(I)}$ co-catalyst
an organoboron reagent ($\text{R}-\text{B(OH)}_2$ or boronate ester) activated by a base
an organotin reagent ($\text{R}-\text{SnBu}_3$) under neutral conditions
questions.explanationEn: The Suzuki-Miyaura reaction couples organoboronic acids/esters with organic halides/triflates in the presence of a $\text{Pd}(0)$ catalyst and a base (which forms a four-coordinate anionic boronate to promote transmetalation). Organotin is Stille, organozinc is Negishi, and terminal alkyne + Cu(I) is Sonogashira.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the active site of carbonic anhydrase, the $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ion is tetrahedrally coordinated by three histidine residues and one water molecule. The primary catalytic role of $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ in hydrating $\text{CO}_2$ to $\text{HCO}_3^-$ is to
optionsEn: act as a Lewis acid that lowers the $\text{p}K_a$ of the coordinated water from $15.7$ to $\sim 7$, generating a nucleophilic $\text{Zn}-\text{OH}^-$ species at physiological pH
bind $\text{CO}_2$ directly as an $\eta^2\text{-CO}_2$ organometallic complex
undergo a $\text{Zn(II)}/\text{Zn(0)}$ redox cycle to reduce $\text{CO}_2$
deprotonate a histidine ring to form a covalent carbamate intermediate
questions.explanationEn: $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$, redox-inactive) functions as a strong Lewis acid in a hydrophobic pocket, lowering the $\text{p}K_a$ of bound $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\approx 6.8\text{--}7.0$. At physiological pH, the resulting zinc-bound hydroxide ($\text{Zn}-\text{OH}^-$) performs nucleophilic attack on $\text{CO}_2$ to yield $\text{Zn}-\text{HCO}_3^-$, which is then displaced by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), the area under an endothermic melting peak in a plot of heat flow ($dH/dt$) versus time (or temperature at a constant heating rate) directly measures
optionsEn: the mass loss of the sample during melting
the enthalpy of fusion ($\Delta H_{\text{fus}}$) of the sample
the activation energy for thermal decomposition
the magnetic susceptibility change at the melting point
questions.explanationEn: DSC measures the difference in heat flow rate ($dQ/dt = dH/dt$ at constant pressure) required to keep the sample and reference at the same temperature. Integrating the heat-flow peak over time directly yields the total enthalpy change ($\Delta H = \int (dH/dt)\,dt$) of the phase transition, such as $\Delta H_{\text{fus}}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following pairs of fragments are ISOLOBAL with each other?
optionsEn: $\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_4$ and $\text{CH}_2$
$\text{Co}(\text{CO})_3$ and $\text{CH}$
$(\eta^5\text{-Cp})\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_2$ and $\text{CH}_3^\bullet$
$\text{Cr}(\text{CO})_5$ and $\text{CH}_3^\bullet$
questions.explanationEn: Using electron deficiency relative to $18\text{ e}^-$ (metal) and $8\text{ e}^-$ (carbon): (A) $\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_4$ ($16\text{ e}^-$, $2$ short) $\leftrightarrow \text{CH}_2$ ($6\text{ e}^-$, $2$ short) — Isolobal. (B) $\text{Co}(\text{CO})_3$ ($15\text{ e}^-$, $3$ short) $\leftrightarrow \text{CH}$ ($5\text{ e}^-$, $3$ short) — Isolobal. (C) $\text{CpFe}(\text{CO})_2$ ($17\text{ e}^-$, $1$ short) $\leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3^\bullet$ ($7\text{ e}^-$, $1$ short) — Isolobal. (D) $\text{Cr}(\text{CO})_5$ ($16\text{ e}^-$, $2$ short) is isolobal with $\text{CH}_2$ (or $\text{CH}_3^+$), NOT $\text{CH}_3^\bullet$. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about radioactive decay processes are CORRECT?
optionsEn: A nuclide with a neutron-to-proton ($N/Z$) ratio ABOVE the belt of stability typically decays by $\beta^-$ emission to decrease $N/Z$
A nuclide with a neutron-to-proton ($N/Z$) ratio BELOW the belt of stability typically decays by $\beta^+$ (positron) emission or electron capture to increase $N/Z$
Gamma ($\gamma$) emission changes neither the mass number $A$ nor the atomic number $Z$ of the nucleus
The half-life $t_{1/2}$ of a first-order radioactive decay depends linearly on the initial amount of the radionuclide
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: neutron-rich nuclei convert a neutron to a proton via $\beta^-$ decay, lowering $N/Z$. (B) True: proton-rich nuclei convert a proton to a neutron via $\beta^+$ decay or electron capture, raising $N/Z$. (C) True: $\gamma$-decay is nuclear de-excitation emitting a high-energy photon without changing $A$ or $Z$. (D) False: radioactive decay is strictly first-order, so $t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda}$ is independent of initial concentration/mass. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the cationic piano-stool complex $[(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_x]^+$ (atomic number of $\text{Fe} = 26$) to obey the $18$-electron rule, the value of $x$ is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Using the neutral-ligand method: $\text{Fe}$ (Group 8) $= 8\text{ e}^-$, $\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5 = 5\text{ e}^-$, $+1$ charge $= -1\text{ e}^-$, and each $\text{CO} = 2\text{ e}^-$. Setting $8 + 5 - 1 + 2x = 18$ gives $12 + 2x = 18 \implies 2x = 6 \implies x = 3$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the resting oxidized $[\text{Fe}_4\text{S}_4(\text{S-Cys})_4]^{2-}$ cluster of a bacterial ferredoxin, the average formal oxidation state of iron is $+x$. The value of $x$ (rounded off to one decimal place) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The cluster contains four inorganic sulfide ligands ($4 \times (-2) = -8$) and four cysteine thiolate ligands ($4 \times (-1) = -4$), for a total ligand charge of $-12$. Since the overall cluster charge is $-2$, the four iron atoms carry a combined charge of $-2 - (-12) = +10$ (corresponding to two $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and two $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ centers delocalized as two $\text{Fe}^{2.5+}$ pairs), giving an average oxidation state of $\frac{+10}{4} = +2.5$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In zero external magnetic field, the number of absorption lines observed in the $^{57}\text{Fe}$ Mössbauer spectrum of $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ is $p$ and that of $\text{FeSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $q$. The sum $p + q$ is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ contains low-spin $\text{Fe(II)}$ ($t_{2g}^6$, spherically symmetric electronic distribution) in a regular $O_h$ ligand field, so the electric field gradient (EFG) is zero and it gives a single line ($p = 1$). High-spin $\text{Fe(II)}$ ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$) in $\text{FeSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has an asymmetric $d$-electron distribution producing a large EFG and quadrupole splitting into a doublet ($q = 2$). Thus $p + q = 1 + 2 = 3$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The associative CO substitution rate of $[(\eta^5\text{-indenyl})\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_2]$ with $\text{PPh}_3$ is approximately $10^8$ times faster than that of $[(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_2]$ (the 'indenyl effect'). This dramatic rate enhancement arises because
optionsEn: the fused benzene ring increases steric bulk around $\text{Rh}$, forcing a dissociative mechanism
$[(\eta^5\text{-indenyl})\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_2]$ is a $16$-electron complex whereas $[(\eta^5\text{-Cp})\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_2]$ is an $18$-electron complex
$\eta^5 \to \eta^3$ ring slippage of the indenyl ligand restores full $6\pi$ Hückel aromaticity in the fused benzene ring, strongly stabilizing the associative transition state
the indenyl ligand dissociates completely as a free anion in the rate-determining step
questions.explanationEn: Associative attack of $\text{PPh}_3$ on an $18$-electron complex requires $\eta^5 \to \eta^3$ hapticity slippage to avoid a $20$-electron transition state. For $\text{Cp}$, $\eta^5 \to \eta^3$ slippage disrupts aromaticity of the $5$-membered ring. For indenyl, slipping from $\eta^5$ to $\eta^3$ localizes the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds so that the fused $6$-membered ring regains full benzene aromatic resonance energy, lowering $\Delta G^\ddagger$ drastically.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Two-electron reduction of $[\text{Re}_2\text{{Cl}}_8]^{2-}$ in the presence of $\text{PMe}_2\text{Ph}$ yields $[\text{Re}_2\text{Cl}_4(\text{PMe}_2\text{Ph})_4]$. Which statement accurately describes the change in $\text{Re}-\text{Re}$ bond order and bond length upon this reduction?
optionsEn: The bond order decreases from $3$ to $1$, yielding a paramagnetic complex with $2$ unpaired electrons
The bond order decreases from $4$ to $2$ ($\sigma^2\pi^2$), lengthening the bond by $> 0.5\text{ \AA}$
The bond order decreases from $4$ ($\sigma^2\pi^4\delta^2$) to $3$ ($\sigma^2\pi^4\delta^2\delta^{*2}$), yet the $\text{Re}-\text{Re}$ bond length remains nearly unchanged ($\approx 2.24\text{ \AA}$)
The bond order increases from $4$ to $5$, shortening the $\text{Re}-\text{Re}$ bond dramatically
questions.explanationEn: In $[\text{Re}_2\text{{Cl}}_8]^{2-}$, two $\text{Re(III)}$ ($d^4$) centers give $8$ $d$-electrons ($\sigma^2\pi^4\delta^2$, $\text{BO} = 4$). In $[\text{Re}_2\text{Cl}_4(\text{PMe}_2\text{Ph})_4]$, two $\text{Re(II)}$ ($d^5$) centers give $10$ $d$-electrons ($\sigma^2\pi^4\delta^2\delta^{*2}$, $\text{BO} = 3$). Because $\delta$ and $\delta^*$ orbitals are very weakly bonding/antibonding (and lower formal charge allows $d$-orbital expansion strengthening $\sigma/\pi$ overlap), the $\text{Re}-\text{Re}$ bond length stays virtually unchanged ($\sim 2.24\text{ \AA}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the Chauvin mechanism of transition-metal-catalyzed olefin metathesis, the key cyclic intermediate formed between the metal-alkylidene ($\text{M}=\text{CHR}$) and an incoming alkene ($\text{R}'\text{CH}=\text{CHR}'$) is a
optionsEn: metallacyclopropene formed via $\alpha$-hydride elimination
$\pi$-allyl metal hydride formed via allylic $\text{C}-\text{H}$ activation
metallacyclobutane formed via reversible $[2+2]$ cycloaddition
metallacyclopentane formed via oxidative cyclization of two alkenes
questions.explanationEn: Chauvin demonstrated that olefin metathesis proceeds by reversible $[2+2]$ cycloaddition of an alkene across a metal-carbene double bond ($\text{M}=\text{C}$) to form a 4-membered **metallacyclobutane** intermediate, followed by retro-$[2+2]$ cycloreversion in the orthogonal sense to release the exchanged alkene and a new metal-carbene.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The limiting biological stoichiometry for the reduction of $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{N}_2$ by molybdenum nitrogenase requires $8\text{ electrons}$, $8\text{ protons}$, and $16\text{ MgATP}$, producing $2\text{ NH}_3$ along with
optionsEn: $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas (obligatory $\text{H}_2$ evolution coupled to reductive elimination of bridging hydrides for $\text{N}_2$ binding)
$2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$ (hydrazine) as the final released product
$0\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas
$1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$ gas
questions.explanationEn: The balanced physiological reaction catalyzed by Mo-nitrogenase is $\text{N}_2 + 8\text{H}^+ + 8\text{e}^- + 16\text{MgATP} \to 2\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2 + 16\text{MgADP} + 16\text{P}_i$. Even under saturating $\text{N}_2$ pressure, at least $1\text{ equiv.}$ of $\text{H}_2$ is obligatorily evolved via reductive elimination of two Fe-bound hydrides on the $E_4$ state, which activates FeMo-co to bind and reduce $\text{N}_2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the EPR spectrum of a square planar $\text{Cu(II)}$ complex coordinated to four equivalent $^{14}\text{N}$ ($I = 1$) donor atoms (e.g., copper(II) phthalocyanine), each of the $4$ copper hyperfine lines ($^{63,65}\text{Cu}$, $I = 3/2$) is further split by superhyperfine coupling to the four equivalent $^{14}\text{N}$ nuclei into
optionsEn: $16$ superhyperfine lines
$5$ superhyperfine lines
$9$ superhyperfine lines
$4$ superhyperfine lines
questions.explanationEn: The number of superhyperfine lines produced by coupling of the unpaired electron to $n$ equivalent ligand nuclei of spin $I$ is $2nI + 1$. For $n = 4$ equivalent $^{14}\text{N}$ nuclei with $I = 1$, each Cu hyperfine line splits into $2(4)(1) + 1 = 9$ superhyperfine lines (giving $4 \times 9 = 36$ lines in total if fully resolved).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
Using Wade-Mingos rules, identify the cluster(s) whose metal framework adopts a *nido* structure ($n + 2$ skeletal electron pairs):
(Atomic numbers: $\text{Fe} = 26$, $\text{Ru} = 44$, $\text{Os} = 76$, $\text{Co} = 27$)
optionsEn: $\text{Fe}_5(\mu_5\text{-C})(\text{CO})_{15}$ (square pyramidal $\text{Fe}_5$ core)
$[\text{Ru}_5(\mu_5\text{-C})(\text{CO})_{15}]$ (square pyramidal $\text{Ru}_5$ core)
$\text{Os}_5(\text{CO})_{16}$ (trigonal bipyramidal $\text{Os}_5$ core)
$[\text{Fe}_4(\mu_4\text{-C})(\text{CO})_{12}]^{2-}$ (butterfly $\text{Fe}_4$ core)
questions.explanationEn: Compute SEPs $= (\text{TVE} - 12n)/2$: (A) $\text{Fe}_5\text{C}(\text{CO})_{15}$ ($n=5$): $\text{TVE} = 5(8) + 4 + 15(2) = 74$; $\text{SEPs} = (74 - 60)/2 = 7 = n + 2$ (*nido* square pyramid, Correct). (B) $\text{Ru}_5\text{C}(\text{CO})_{15}$ is isoelectronic ($74\text{ e}^-$, $7$ SEPs $= n+2$, *nido* square pyramid, Correct). (C) $\text{Os}_5(\text{CO})_{16}$ ($n=5$): $\text{TVE} = 72$, $\text{SEPs} = 6 = n+1$ (*closo* trigonal bipyramid, Incorrect). (D) $[\text{Fe}_4\text{C}(\text{CO})_{12}]^{2-}$ ($n=4$): $\text{TVE} = 4(8) + 4 + 24 + 2 = 62$; $\text{SEPs} = (62 - 48)/2 = 7 = n + 3$ (*arachno* butterfly, Incorrect). Hence (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following physiological factors shift the $\text{O}_2$ binding curve of hemoglobin to the RIGHT (increasing $P_{50}$, lowering $\text{O}_2$ affinity, and promoting $\text{O}_2$ release to tissues)?
optionsEn: Decrease in blood pH (increase in $[\text{H}^+]$, the Bohr effect)
Increase in the concentration of $2,3$-bisphosphoglycerate ($2,3$-BPG), which binds electrostatically in the central cavity of T-state deoxy-Hb
Increase in partial pressure of $\text{CO}_2$ (forming carbamate adducts at N-termini and lowering pH)
Binding of carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) to one heme subunit of hemoglobin
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: lower pH stabilizes T-state salt bridges, shifting the curve right. (B) True: polyanionic $2,3$-BPG binds exclusively to positively charged residues in the central cavity of T-state Hb, shifting the curve right. (C) True: elevated $\text{CO}_2$ lowers pH and forms T-state-stabilizing carbamates, shifting the curve right. (D) False: $\text{CO}$ locks Hb in the high-affinity R-state, shifting the curve to the LEFT and preventing $\text{O}_2$ release to tissues! Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The neutral interstitial carbide cluster $\text{Ru}_6(\mu_6\text{-C})(\text{CO})_x$ adopts a *closo* octahedral $\text{Ru}_6$ core according to Wade-Mingos rules ($n + 1 = 7$ skeletal electron pairs). Given that $\text{Ru}$ is a Group $8$ metal and the interstitial carbon contributes $4$ valence electrons, the integer value of $x$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: For a $6$-vertex *closo* octahedral cluster ($n = 6$), the required total valence electron count is $12n + 2(n + 1) = 14n + 2 = 14(6) + 2 = 86\text{ e}^-$. Setting $6(8) + 4 + 2x = 86$ gives $52 + 2x = 86 \implies 2x = 34 \implies x = 17$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Let $n_1$, $n_2$, and $n_3$ be the number of unpaired electrons per iron center in deoxy-myoglobin, oxy-myoglobin, and aquomet-myoglobin (high-spin $\text{Fe(III)}$), respectively. The sum $n_1 + n_2 + n_3$ is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: In deoxy-myoglobin, the 5-coordinate $\text{Fe(II)}$ ($d^6$) is high-spin, giving $n_1 = 4$ unpaired electrons. In oxy-myoglobin, the $\text{Fe(III)}-\text{O}_2^{\bullet -}$ unit is strongly antiferromagnetically coupled and diamagnetic, giving $n_2 = 0$. In aquomet-myoglobin (weak-field axial $\text{H}_2\text{O}$), $\text{Fe(III)}$ ($d^5$) is high-spin, giving $n_3 = 5$. Therefore, $n_1 + n_2 + n_3 = 4 + 0 + 5 = 9$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
When pure $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$ is heated to $550\,^\circ\text{C}$ in a thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA), it loses $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{CO}$ quantitatively to form solid $\text{CaCO}_3$. The percentage of the original sample mass remaining at $550\,^\circ\text{C}$ is _______ $\%$ (rounded off to two decimal places).
(Given atomic masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{H} = 1.0$, $\text{C} = 12.0$, $\text{O} = 16.0$, $\text{Ca} = 40.0$)
questions.explanationEn: The molar mass of $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $40.0 + 2(12.0) + 4(16.0) + 18.0 = 146.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$. After losing $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) and $\text{CO}$ ($28.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$), the solid residue is $\text{CaCO}_3$ with molar mass $40.0 + 12.0 + 3(16.0) = 100.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$. Therefore, the percentage mass remaining is $\frac{100.0}{146.0} \times 100\% = 68.4932\% \approx 68.49\%$.
